Scene: United Yharmin before its downfall. One immense great keep, with a single towering central stronghold of black medieval stone and subtle weathered gold ornament, rises above a misty unified kingdom. A lone distant High King appears as a small regal silhouette on a central balcony, framed by a tall arch and warm gold backlight. The crown has a simple ancient design with five long tapering points. The king and the central keep are the unmistakable focus. A few terraces, bridges and faint settlements descend into mist, implying peace and unity without distracting from the central scene. Pale ancient sunlight, dignified grandeur, a poignant feeling of a lost golden age. Wide view with the keep occupying the central half, lower foreground disappearing into dark cloud.

Scene: The same ancient great keep is breached in a single terrible night. Its colossal pointed-arch gate, built from charcoal black stone with weathered narrow gold bands, has burst inward. Broken gate timbers and shattered masonry fall around the central opening. Shadowy invading soldiers push through the breach as tiny ominous silhouettes at the center, amid drifting sparks and storm-driven smoke. No close-up character or gore. A stormy cold ash-blue night clashes with dull ochre ember glow coming from within the gate. Let the huge breached gate dominate the central 50 percent of the composition, conveying the collapse of an ancient kingdom in one instant. Lower foreground dark and quiet, no detailed soldiers near the bottom.

Scene: The crown is lost. Close, low, intimate view of an abandoned ancient gold crown, with five long tapering points and engraved weathering but no gems or symbols, tipped on its side upon cracked black throne-room flagstones. The crown is slightly below the image center but above the dark bottom quarter, entirely within the central half of the canvas. Dust, ash and a few tiny stone fragments surround it. A narrow shaft of faint tarnished gold light from a ruined high window illuminates the crown while the immense empty throne behind is indistinct in deep shadow. No person, hand, corpse or body. The crown feels small and vulnerable against the vast ruined chamber; lonely, sacred, final. Tactile brush marks, restrained luminous gold metal.

Scene: A kingdom divided after the crown is lost. A monumental empty broken throne of black stone stands at the center of a ruined pointed-arch great hall. A large diagonal fracture crosses the vacant throne; its worn gold inlay barely catches the light. Several rival house leaders, about five, stand in separate shadowed positions around the throne in the middle half of the frame, as small cloaked silhouettes facing it and each other with distrust. Their identities are ambiguous and original. Each remains visibly separate with empty space between them. Plain tattered muted-color heraldic banners without any symbols or text hang deep in the background. Fractured shafts of cold ash light cut down through the broken ceiling, tiny glints of old gold remain. Convey authority lost and unity fractured; solemn quiet tension, no fighting or gore. The lowest quarter dissolves into dark floor shadow.
